text: Raju purchased an item for ₹ 8200 and sold it at a gain of 25%. From that amount he purchased another item and sold it at a loss of 20%. What is his overall gain/loss?
explanation: SP₁ = 8200 × 125/100 = ₹ 10250. He buys 2nd item for ₹ 10250. SP₂ = 10250 × 80/100 = ₹ 8200. Since initial investment = final amount, neither gain nor loss.

text: A property dealer sells a house for ₹ 6,30,000 and in the bargain makes a profit of 5%. Had he sold it for ₹ 5,00,000, then what percentage of loss or gain he would have made?

Ashok buys a car at 20% discount of the price and sells it at 20% higher price. His percentage gain is
explanation: Let original price = 100. He buys at 80 (20% discount) and sells at 120 (20% higher). Gain = 40. Gain% = (40/80) × 100 = 50%.

text: At what profit percent must an article be sold so that by selling at half that price, there may be a loss of 30%?
explanation: Let CP = 100. At half the selling price, loss = 30%, so half SP = 70, meaning SP = 140. Profit = 140 − 100 = 40. Profit% = 40%.

text: In a certain store, the profit is 320% of the cost. If the cost increases by 25% but the selling price remains constant, approximately what percentage of the selling price is the profit?
explanation: Let CP = 100. Profit = 320, SP = 420. New CP = 125. New Profit = 420 − 125 = 295. Profit as % of SP = (295/420) × 100 ≈ 70%.

Manish purchased 25 kg of rice @ ₹ 32 per kg and 15 kg of rice @ ₹ 36 per kg. He mixed the two varieties of rice and sold it @ ₹ 40.20 per kg. What is the percent profit earned?

Arun purchased 30 kg of wheat at the rate of ₹ 11.50 per kg and 20 kg of wheat at the rate of ₹ 14.25 per kg. He mixed the two and sold the mixture. Approximately what price per kg should he sell the mixture to make 30% profit?

A trader mixes three varieties of groundnuts costing ₹ 50, ₹ 20 and ₹ 30 per kg in the ratio 2 : 4 : 3 in terms of weight, and sells the mixture at ₹ 33 per kg. What percentage of profit does he make?

The manufacturer of a certain item can sell all he can produce at the selling price of ₹ 60 each. It costs him ₹ 40 in materials and labour to produce each item and he has overhead expenses of ₹ 3000 per week. The number of units he should produce and sell to make a profit of at least ₹ 1000 per week is
explanation: Profit per unit = 60 − 40 = ₹ 20. Total profit needed = 1000 + 3000 (overhead) = ₹ 4000. Units = 4000/20 = 200.

text: A dealer buys dry fruit at the rate of ₹ 100, ₹ 80 and ₹ 60 per kg. He bought them in the ratio 12 : 15 : 20 by weight. He gets 20% profit by selling the first two quantities and finds he has no gain no loss on the whole. What was the percentage loss he suffered for the third quantity?

A milkman cheats his customer in two ways. He mixes 10% water in pure milk and increases the price of milk by 10%. He purchases 20 kg pure milk at a rate of ₹ 15 per kg. His total profit by selling it is
explanation: CP = 20 × 15 = ₹ 300. With 10% water, he has 22 kg mixture. SP per kg = 110% of 15 = ₹ 16.50. Total SP = 22 × 16.50 = ₹ 363. Profit = 363 − 300 = ₹ 63.

text: A dishonest dealer uses a scale of 90 cm instead of a metre scale and claims to sell at cost price. His profit is
explanation: He gives 90 cm worth of goods but charges for 100 cm. Gain = 10 cm. Gain% = (10/90) × 100 = 11⅑%.

text: A dishonest dealer professes to sell his goods at cost price. But he uses a false weight and thus gains 6 18/47%. For a kg, he uses a weight of
explanation: Gain% = 300/47%. Let actual weight = w gm. Then (1000 − w)/w × 100 = 300/47. Solving: 47000 − 47w = 3w → 50w = 47000 → w = 940 gms.

text: A fruit seller professes to sell his fruits at cost price, but still gains 25% on his outlay. What weight does he substitute for a kilogram?
explanation: He gains 25% by giving less weight. Actual weight = 1000 × 100/125 = 800 gm.

text: A shopkeeper cheats to the extent of 10% while buying as well as selling, by using false weights. His total gain is
explanation: While buying he gets 10% more, while selling he gives 10% less. Total gain% = 10 + 10 + (10 × 10)/100 = 21%.

text: Left pan of a faulty balance weighs 100 grams more than its right pan. A shopkeeper keeps the weight in the left pan while buying but in the right pan while selling. He uses only 1 kg weight measure. If he sells his goods at the listed cost price, what is his gain?
explanation: While buying: gets 1100g for 1000g price. While selling: gives 900g for 1000g price. From 1100g, revenue = (1100/900) × cost. Gain% = (200/900) × 100 = 200/9 %.

text: A grocer sells rice at a profit of 10% and uses weights which are 20% less than the market weight. The total gain earned by him will be
explanation: He buys 1 kg for ₹ 100. Sells at 10% profit = ₹ 110 per 'kg'. But gives only 800g (20% less). Effectively: buys 1000g for 100, sells 1000g for (1000/800) × 110 = ₹ 137.50. But gain on investment = (110 − 80)/100 × (100/80) = 30%.

text: A merchant professes to lose 4% on a certain tea but he uses a weight equal to 840g instead of 1 kg. Find his real loss or gain percent.
explanation: SP of 1 kg = 96% of CP (4% loss claimed). But he gives only 840g. Actual CP of 840g = 84% of CP per kg. Gain% = (96 − 84)/84 × 100 = 12/84 × 100 = 100/7 = 14²⁄₇% gain.

text: A shopkeeper advertises for selling cloth at 4% loss. However, by using a false metre scale he actually gains 20%. What is the actual length of the scale?
explanation: Let actual scale = L cm. He sells L cm at price of 100 cm at 4% loss. So 96/L = 120/100 (20% gain). L = 96 × 100/120 = 80 cm.

text: A trader professes to sell his goods at a nominal gain percentage but actually earns 37½% profit by using false weight. If for a kg he uses a weight of 800 gm, what is the nominal gain percentage at which he claims to be selling his goods?
explanation: Let nominal gain = x%. He gives 800g but charges for 1000g at (100+x)% of cost. Actual gain = (1000/800)(100+x)/100 − 1 = 37.5%. So 1.25(100+x)/100 = 1.375. (100+x) = 110. x = 10%.

text: Prateek sold a music system to Kartik at 20% gain and Kartik sold it to Swastik at 40% gain. If Swastik paid ₹ 10500 for the music system, what amount did Prateek pay for the same?
explanation: Swastik paid ₹ 10500 = 140% of Kartik's CP. Kartik's CP = 10500/1.4 = ₹ 7500 = 120% of Prateek's CP. Prateek's CP = 7500/1.2 = ₹ 6250.

text: A manufacturer sells an article to a wholesale dealer at a profit of 20% and the wholesale dealer sells it to a retail merchant at a loss of 5%. Find the resultant loss or profit.
explanation: Let manufacturer's CP = 100. Wholesaler buys at 120. Retailer buys at 95% of 120 = 114. Net effect = 14% gain on original cost.

Net for X = 157500 − 154350 + (150000 − 157500) = X spent 150000, got 157500, then bought back at 154350. Net gain = 157500 − 150000 − (154350 − 157500) = 7500 − (−3150) wait let me recalc. text: The cost of manufacturing an article rose by 18% as a result of the increase in the cost of raw material. A manufacturer revised the selling price of the article so as to maintain the same profit percentage as before. He found that now he got ₹ 9 more than the earlier profit by selling each article. What was the earlier profit per article?
explanation: Let original CP = 100, profit% = P. New CP = 118. Same profit%, so new profit = 118P/100. Increase = 18P/100 = 9. So P = 50. Earlier profit = ₹ 50.

text: An article passing through two hands is sold at a profit of 38% at the original cost price. If the first dealer makes a profit of 20%, then the profit percent made by the second dealer is
explanation: Let original CP = 100. Final SP = 138. First dealer's SP = 120. Second dealer's profit = 138 − 120 = 18. Profit% = (18/120) × 100 = 15%.

text: Vineet calculates his profit percentage on the selling price whereas Roshan calculates his profit on the cost price. They find that the difference of their profits is ₹ 275. If the selling price of both is the same, Vineet gets 25% profit and Roshan gets 15% profit. Find their selling price.
explanation: Let SP = x. Vineet's profit = 25% of x = x/4. Roshan's CP = x/1.15, profit = x − x/1.15 = 15x/115 = 3x/23. Difference = x/4 − 3x/23 = (23x − 12x)/92 = 11x/92 = 275. So x = 275 × 92/11 = ₹ 2300.

explanation: Let CP = 100. Required SP = 120 (20% gain). SP = 90% of MP = 120. MP = 120/0.9 = 133.33. Mark-up = 33⅓% above CP.

explanation: Let list price = 100. Komal buys at 75 (25% discount). He wants profit of 25% on 100 = ₹ 25. SP = 100 + 25 = 125. Markup on his cost = (125 − 75)/75 × 100 = 66.67%.
